title: Not realistic
body:
How possible this

If you mean 1 lakh (100,000) steps in one day, the distance depends on your stride length.

On average:

* 1 step ≈ 0.75 to 0.80 metres
* 100,000 steps ≈ 75–80 km

A quick estimate:

* 100,000 × 0.75 m = 75,000 m = 75 km
* 100,000 × 0.80 m = 80,000 m = 80 km

So, 1 lakh steps is approximately 75–80 kilometres for most adults.

but for most people it is extremely difficult and not practical to do every day in 1L steps!!!!!
If 1L steps on everyday means 

* 100,000 steps ≈ 75–80 km of walking.
* At a normal walking speed of 5 km/h, it would take about 15–16 hours of continuous walking (not including breaks).

My opinion is

For general health, 7,000–10,000 steps per day is a realistic and beneficial target for many adults, though the ideal goal depends on your age, fitness level, and health.

So it’s fully scam recorded steps and achievements 

So plz tell me anyone is it correct challenge????

title: Works great but doesn’t sync with Apple Health
body:
Everything is great about this app. Tracks steps, running, cycling and all other forms of fitness, however you have to turn the respective health feature on.. in order for the app to track it.

The only area of concern is that the tracks separate steps count apart from what I get on Apple health and on my iWatch. The data from apple health and iWatch is more accurate and doesn’t sync with the Samsung health app data count. In spite of you trying to manually sync it, there are discrepancies on every day count between the two systems. 

In addition, I can’t keep carrying the phone whenever I run or cycle, hence I wear a smart watch. You have to develop an app that tracks the fitness workout through the watch as well. If there is such an app function available for iPhone and iWatch users it makes sense to disregard the apple health data and go with Samsung health.
